---
title: "AI use rules"
date: last-modified
---

What you put into AI is sorted like a traffic light. The AI policies of the university and of the journal you will submit to always come first.

# Traffic light {#traffic-light}

| Signal | What it covers |
|---|---|
| Free to use | Explanations of concepts and grammar, help with reading published papers, track B manuscripts |
| Always verify | References, numbers, suggested statistical methods, recent research findings, whether a sentence that AI revised still means the same thing |
| Conditional (track A) | Sentences from your own manuscript. Get your supervisor's agreement. Use only tools set so that your input is not used for training. Do not put in raw data or figure files |
| Do not put in | Patient information, manuscripts under review (including other people's manuscripts you received as a reviewer), ideas not yet filed in a grant or patent, account details |

The research ethics guide of Kyungpook National University says not to put unpublished research data into AI. For practice in this course, the "Conditional (track A)" row is allowed. You must meet all of its conditions.

If you are unsure whether something may go into AI, ask the instructor before you put it in.

# The three checks {#three-checks}

Check the source
: Check references and numbers yourself in PubMed, through the DOI, or in the paper.

Cross-check
: Check with textbooks, review papers, peers and the instructor.

Read side by side
: Put the sentence that AI revised next to your original sentence, and check that the claims and numbers have not changed.

# When you write the paper {#in-the-paper}

- AI cannot be an author. The authors are responsible for the paper.
- State that you used AI in the Methods or the Acknowledgments, as the journal's policy requires.
- Do not use AI to make or edit data figures (blots, micrographs and so on).

# AI use log {#ai-log}
